content.text:
**Here are the 5 most notable recent tweets** (from the last 24 hours, as of Aug 16, 2026) discussing x402 payment protocol security vulnerabilities and related topics like AI/agent dispute resolution or trust layers:

- **@402Signal** (Ross): Highlighted key USENIX Security ’26 research testing 15 x402 facilitators (covering 99% of observed txs) and uncovering 31 previously unknown vulnerabilities in verification/settlement (e.g., free shopping, gas abuse, service denial). Noted that Coinbase, PayAI, and Mogami have confirmed fixes; emphasized the growing blast radius as facilitators become shared infrastructure.[[1]](https://x.com/402Signal/status/2088808680347013525)

- **@drewszarka** (lowercase.base.eth): Reported on a CoinDesk-covered study showing Coinbase and 14 other x402 facilitators failing security tests for the AI-agent economy. Detailed risks like merchants left unpaid, facilitator asset exposure, and the “free shopping” attack (where off-chain verification passes but on-chain settlement fails, allowing irreversible services). Suggested solutions from @usefinal, @FlexaHQ, and @ampdotxyz.[[2]](https://x.com/drewszarka/status/2088602693216395281)

- **@VU_virtuals** (Velvet Unicorn): Noted that x402 facilitators have surfaced 31 vulnerabilities across 15 major implementations (including Coinbase) just as the agent-payments stack enters production. Framed this alongside agent liability, identity registries, and the shift from “can it pay?” to “who is accountable?” in the AI-agent economy.[[3]](https://x.com/VU_virtuals/status/2088747810719994220)

- **@33xp_** (riot'): Discussed x402’s 162Mth payment milestone alongside emerging bugs in the agent tooling layer and a study showing up to 90.6% of ERC-8004 reviewers as coordinated fakes (sybil attacks). Warned that the “security layer” and “trust layer” are the weakest points, predicting the first major agent-economy failure could be a security incident or trust collapse rather than liquidity.[[4]](https://x.com/33xp_/status/2088915992336347639)

- **@OpenPengu** (Open Pengu｜企鵝開講): Addressed the shift to AI agents arguing over contracts/disputes, noting x402 handles payments but identity, registries, and trust scores will decide accountability. Posed the question of whether the judgment layer should use verifiable execution history, a human appeal path, or both—directly touching on AI-judged or hybrid dispute resolution.[[5]](https://x.com/OpenPengu/status/2088961164600557992)

These posts stand out for their direct engagement with the security research findings and emerging trust/dispute issues in x402/agent payments. No other highly notable tweets matched the exact criteria in the results.
